decisions.boundary_condition: Apply this only when comparing connecting itineraries; do not infer a general preference for either nonstop flights or flights with a layover.
decisions.canonical_value: For connecting itineraries, prefer at most one short, practical layover.
decisions.condition: When evaluating flight itineraries with connections.
decisions.default_action: Prioritize itineraries with at most one layover and a short connection that permits a practical transfer and brief break.
decisions.exception_condition: Follow explicit current-trip requirements for a different number or duration of stops.
decisions.name: flight_connection_limit_preference
decisions.preference_value: When a flight connection is needed, prefer no more than one short layover.
decisions.rationale: Multiple examples support a soft limit of at most one layover and a preference for a short, practical connection when a connecting itinerary is considered. The evidence does not justify inferring that a connection is preferred over nonstop service.

decisions.boundary_condition: Treat business class as a soft preference, not a requirement, and do not infer an independent standing budget or price threshold.
decisions.canonical_value: Prefer business class when feasible, with coach as the fallback.
decisions.default_action: Prefer or surface business-class options first.
decisions.exception_condition: Use coach when business class is unavailable, infeasible under explicit current-trip constraints, or declined by the user.
decisions.name: prefer_business_class_with_coach_fallback
decisions.preference_value: Prefer business class when available and feasible, with coach acceptable as a fallback.
decisions.rationale: Repeated examples support business class as a soft cabin preference, while one example explicitly establishes coach as the fallback. Budget feasibility remains a current-trip constraint rather than a persistent price rule.
